audit.why: 7/10 with Cassiopeia owning Levels 4-5 and 2+ items is right: 850-range Noxious Blast and a 0.75s Twin Fang against a 300-range Chomp means she picks the range, and the only stage Trundle truly owns is level 1 before poison stacks.
The four windows — level 1 Chomp, her level 6 Petrifying Gaze, her first AP item, and your late Subjugate MR drain — are the right four and the level-6 flag is the correct one to raise.
audit.corrected: Sharpened the level-6 spike to state the actual facing rule instead of a vague 'approach from the side'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Chomp is twice said to slow her ATTACK SPEED; it saps Attack Damage and slows movement. (b) wants.you[2] says Pillar of Ice can 'interrupt her grounding zone', and breakdown/mid says Miasma's grounding 'only matters if she can root you inside it, which your Pillar disrupts'. Pillar of Ice removes nothing and Miasma roots nobody. (c) The grounding is treated as a threat when it is nearly free against Trundle — grounding disables Movement abilities and Trundle has none, so only the slow costs him anything.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon. Miasma: 'slowing, grounding, and lightly damaging enemies that pass through them. Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities.' Trundle's kit is Chomp (targeted), Frozen Domain (ground zone), Pillar of Ice (ground zone), Subjugate (targeted) — no movement ability in the set. Chomp: 'briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage'. Petrifying Gaze: 'stunning any enemies in front of her that are facing her and slowing any others with their back turned' — the facing rule is the whole level-6 fight. Twin Fang: 0.75s cooldown and it 'heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt', which is the anti-heal cue the interaction file flags.
audit.corrected: Chomp corrected to AD sap; the fabricated 'Pillar interrupts Miasma' removed; grounding re-cast as the free half of Miasma with the slow named as the real cost; the turn-your-back rule on Petrifying Gaze stated outright; Twin Fang's heal named.

audit.whatIsWrong: Miasma is the tracked ability on nine lines with no duration ever given.
audit.why: Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16 — the longest cooldown in her kit by a distance, and 24 seconds at rank 1 is a very large window to walk her down in. Petrifying Gaze is 120/100/80, Noxious Blast 3.5s, Twin Fang 0.75s.
audit.corrected: 24s and 0.75s now stated in the cooldown block, the dos and the report.

edits.before: At level 1 you are the aggressor — Q Chomp on the first auto steals her Attack Damage and slows her attack speed, so do not sit back and let her establish a poke pattern with Noxious Blast. Step onto Frozen Domain W and walk up for a second Chomp the moment Q resets; she has no mobility and every second of extended auto-trading shifts further in your favour. Your passive King's Tribute heals off every minion that dies nearby, meaning her early poison ticks do not accumulate the way they do against immobile tanks — you regenerate faster than she can whittle. The real threat is her W Miasma grounding zone: she will drop it in front of you to slow your advance and trigger Twin Fang chains from poison. Respect the Miasma placement and path around it rather than running into the ground effect.
edits.after: At level 1 you are the aggressor — Q Chomp on the first auto saps her Attack Damage and slows her, so do not sit back and let her establish a poke pattern with Noxious Blast. Step onto Frozen Domain W and walk up for a second Chomp the moment Q resets; she has no mobility and every second of extended auto-trading shifts further in your favour. Your passive King's Tribute heals off every minion that dies nearby, meaning her early poison ticks do not accumulate the way they do against immobile tanks — you regenerate faster than she can whittle. Her answer is Twin Fang on a 0.75-second cooldown, which heals her for a share of the damage it deals to a poisoned target, so Grievous Wounds buys you more than armour does. Respect the Miasma placement and path around the slow instead of walking through it.

edits.before: Once Cassiopeia hits level 6 the dynamic shifts sharply. Her R Petrifying Gaze turns any straight-line approach into a kill opportunity for her — if you walk directly at her face-on, she stuns you and chains Twin Fang at maximum damage. To engage safely, place your Pillar of Ice E first to force her sideways or cut off her retreat, then charge in from the side so she cannot face you for the stun angle. Frozen Domain W should be pre-placed so the ice zone covers the terrain your Pillar creates — she has no dash and Miasma grounding only matters if she can root you inside it, which your Pillar disrupts. At level 6 your Subjugate R drains a flat percentage of her Magic Resistance, which is meaningful even if her resistances are not extreme — it shaves her effective HP and makes your physical follow-up hurt more. The lane is a skill contest through levels 4 to 6: you win the pure stat-trade if you negate the stun, she wins if she face-stuns you.

notes: Only 79 games in the packet — smallest sample in the slice, so the 58.23% figure is soft; treated the kit facts as the authority and left the ratings alone. Killed the fabricated claim that Pillar of Ice can 'interrupt her grounding zone' and the claim that Miasma roots. The genuinely useful and previously missing point is the reverse of what the page said: Miasma grounds Movement abilities, Trundle has none, so the grounding half of her W is free and only the slow costs him. Also stated Petrifying Gaze's facing rule (stun if facing, slow if back turned) which is in Riot's own text and was the missing decisive interaction at 6. One more 'attack speed' Chomp error killed.
